title: Interruptions: Stash and Worktrees
intro: You're halfway through a feature when production breaks. You need a clean checkout of main right now, without losing or committing half-finished work. Stash is the quick answer; worktrees are the better one for anything longer than a few minutes.

steps.prompt: Shelve your uncommitted work, including new untracked files, with the message 'wip: audit log'.
steps.fake_output: Saved working directory and index state On feature/audit-log: wip: audit log
steps.explanation: The working tree is clean, and your changes are saved on the stash.
steps.why: Without -u, new files that were never added are left behind in the working tree, and can end up in the hotfix by accident. A message matters: 'stash@{3}: WIP on main' tells you nothing a week later.

steps.fake_output:
stash@{0}: On feature/audit-log: wip: audit log
stash@{1}: WIP on main: 3e1f0a9 Merge pull request #212
steps.explanation: Two entries; the newest is stash@{0}.
steps.why: The stash is a stack, and old entries pile up and get forgotten. If a stash has been there more than a day, it should have been a commit on a branch.

steps.prompt: After the hotfix, bring your work back. Restore the latest stash but keep it on the stack until you've checked nothing conflicted.
steps.fake_output:
On branch feature/audit-log
Changes not staged for commit:
	modified:   src/audit.py
Untracked files:
	migrations/0042_audit_log.sql
steps.explanation: Your changes are back, and the stash entry still exists.
steps.why: 'pop' applies and deletes in one step; if the apply hits a conflict you're left sorting it out mid-way. 'apply' keeps the entry as a backup, and you 'git stash drop' it once you're happy.

steps.prompt: A better tool for interruptions: check out main in a second directory, ../shop-hotfix, alongside your current work.
steps.fake_output:
Preparing worktree (checking out 'main')
HEAD is now at b7c8d9e Merge pull request #213
steps.explanation: A second working directory on main, sharing the same repository.
steps.why: A worktree gives you two branches checked out at once with one .git directory: no stashing, no half-built state, and your editor and dev server for the feature keep running. It's much faster than a second clone and shares all objects.

steps.prompt: List the worktrees attached to this repository.
steps.explanation: Two directories, each on its own branch.
steps.why: A branch can only be checked out in one worktree at a time, which prevents two directories fighting over the same branch.

steps.prompt: The hotfix is merged. Remove the ../shop-hotfix worktree.
steps.fake_output: (no output: the worktree directory is removed)
steps.explanation: The extra directory and its bookkeeping are gone; the commits remain in the repository.
steps.why: Use 'worktree remove' rather than deleting the folder: it cleans up Git's record of it. If a folder was deleted by hand, 'git worktree prune' tidies up.
